question: What process was discovered in the early 1990s that is currently used to remove ammonia from wastewater and contributes significantly to the loss of fixed nitrogen from the oceans?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anammox**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Anammox (Anaerobic Ammonium Oxidation)** is a biological process that was discovered in the early 1990s.

• This process is used to remove ammonia from wastewater by converting it into nitrogen gas under anaerobic conditions.

• Anammox bacteria are capable of oxidizing ammonium using nitrite as an electron acceptor, producing nitrogen gas.

• Anammox contributes significantly to the loss of fixed nitrogen in marine ecosystems, especially in oxygen-depleted zones.

• It is a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative to traditional nitrogen removal methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Nitrogen Cycle:**

• The nitrogen cycle is a biogeochemical process that transforms nitrogen into various chemical forms, including ammonium, nitrite, nitrate, and nitrogen gas.

• Anammox plays a key role in the nitrogen cycle by converting fixed nitrogen compounds back into atmospheric nitrogen.

• **Anammox Bacteria:**

• Anammox bacteria belong to the Planctomycetes phylum and thrive in anaerobic environments such as wastewater treatment plants and marine sediments.

• Their unique cell structure contains a special organelle known as the "anammoxosome," where the process occurs.

• **Environmental Impact:**

• Anammox reduces the need for chemical additives in wastewater treatment, lowering operational costs and environmental pollution.

• It helps mitigate eutrophication in aquatic ecosystems by reducing nitrogen runoff into water bodies.

• **Applications in Industry:**

• Anammox technology is widely used in modern wastewater treatment systems for nitrogen removal.

• Its adoption has grown due to its high efficiency and sustainability compared to conventional processes like nitrification-denitrification.
